title: Three ways to build the chosen Figma toolbar
brief: Implement the already-selected V1 Figma-style toolbar in SystemSketch: seven stable family slots (Cursor, Frame, Shape, Draw, Text, Comment, +), a family icon that becomes the last selected subtype, R/O/L direct selection, repeated A cycling Straight → Curve → Elbow while remembering the last arrow preset, and a searchable library sidebar. Keep the visible behavior fixed and compare only the technical boundary.
defaultWhy: P1 Compose Upstream is the provisional recommendation at 91/100. It uses tldraw 5.3.2's public DefaultToolbar, responsive OverflowingToolbar behavior, toolbar/menu primitives, useTools registry, built-in keyboard routing, style state, accessibility announcements, and editor side effects. SystemSketch owns only the seven family-slot projection, a tiny preference store, one guarded curved-arrow preset adapter, and the searchable library contents.
decisionHinge: The choice is close between P1 and P2. Moving only 5 weight points from tldraw reuse to pixel/interaction exactness changes the weights to 30/30/20/10/10 and ties them at 90. Choose P2 if eliminating DefaultToolbar's extra chrome and internal CSS dependencies matters more than maximizing upstream composition; otherwise choose P1.
invariants: The rendered toolbar is the chosen V1 Figma surface in every plan; this comparison does not reopen position, icon count, or grouping.
Cursor, Frame, Shape, Draw, Text, Comment, and + occupy seven stable bottom-center positions.
The Shape family slot displays the actual last-used subtype after R, O, L, or an arrow choice.
A recalls the last arrow preset when entering Arrow and cycles Straight → Curve → Elbow only when Arrow is already active.
The + control opens a searchable library surface without changing the selected drawing tool.
Current tool/style state stays in tldraw; family recall is user-interface preference state, never board document data.
The existing Excalidraw paste adapter, bottom-right utility strip, persistence key, release flow, and stock canvas engine remain intact.
All integrations target public tldraw 5.3.2 exports and editor APIs; no package fork or node_modules patch is permitted.
boundary: These are implementation plans and interactive architecture traces, not a toolbar implementation. They identify concrete files, API seams, slices, acceptance evidence, and failure modes. No production React, CSS, editor, or package dependency was changed while preparing this comparison.

axes.name: Toolbar shell
values: SystemSketch catalog over custom tool states

requirements.name: Off-the-shelf tldraw reuse
requirements.why: The requested preference is to lean as hard as practical on tldraw's existing UI, tool, shortcut, style, focus, and responsive infrastructure.
requirements.passCondition: The plan delegates common toolbar behavior to public tldraw components and registries, with custom code limited to behavior that does not exist upstream.

anchors.1: Reimplements toolbar, shortcuts, selection, menus, and tool execution independently of tldraw.
anchors.3: Uses tldraw's editor and tools but owns substantial toolbar or tool-state behavior.
anchors.5: Composes DefaultToolbar, tool items, keyboard routing, styles, focus, and editor behavior directly.

requirements.name: Exact V1 behavior
requirements.why: The interaction model is already chosen; implementation economy is not useful if the result drifts from Figma-style stable family slots and repeated-key behavior.
requirements.passCondition: The seven-slot silhouette, selected subtype feedback, family recall, repeat-A contract, and library sidebar behave exactly as specified.

anchors.1: Requires visible compromises or substitutes a stock individual-tool row.
anchors.3: Matches the core behavior with one or two constrained visual differences.
anchors.5: The implementation boundary imposes no visible or interaction compromise.

requirements.name: Public-API upgrade safety
requirements.why: SystemSketch pins tldraw but should still be able to upgrade without carrying a fork or depending on copied internal state-machine code.
requirements.passCondition: All imports are public, internal CSS/DOM coupling is minimized and documented, and a tldraw version bump has a focused regression surface.

anchors.1: Copies or patches internal tldraw implementation details with broad upgrade exposure.
anchors.3: Uses public registration seams but mirrors some upstream interaction behavior.
anchors.5: Uses only narrow public APIs behind one adapter boundary.

requirements.name: Testability and state clarity
requirements.why: Repeat-key state, family memory, editor state, and document content must not blur together or become regression-prone.
requirements.passCondition: The arrow transition table and preference model are pure-testable, editor effects are guarded, and the full keyboard journey is observable in a real browser.

anchors.1: Behavior emerges from distributed component state and global listeners.
anchors.3: Core transitions are testable but browser/editor coupling remains broad.
anchors.5: State ownership is explicit and each effect has a focused unit or journey proof.

requirements.name: Delivery speed and code volume
requirements.why: The first implementation should close one vertical toolbar behavior without turning into a second UI framework.
requirements.passCondition: A thin first slice can ship Cursor/Frame/Shape/Draw/Text through real tldraw tools, followed by arrow presets, library insertion, and Comment gating.

anchors.1: Requires a new tool framework or large up-front platform layer.
anchors.3: Requires a moderate owned shell/controller before the first complete journey.
anchors.5: Mostly composes existing pieces and adds narrow adapters incrementally.

hardGates.name: Fixed seven-slot V1 surface
hardGates.why: The selected visual and interaction direction must not be reinterpreted during implementation.

hardGates.name: R / O / L / repeated-A plus recall
hardGates.why: The Excalidraw-like keyboard loop and persistent subtype feedback are the primary behavior, not decoration.

hardGates.name: Searchable + library
hardGates.why: The compact toolbar depends on a scalable home for less-frequent objects and templates.

hardGates.name: No tldraw fork or document-schema pollution
hardGates.why: Toolbar preference is UI state and must not create a second editor or leak into shared board content.

hardGates.name: Typing and accessibility safety
hardGates.why: Tool hotkeys must stop while editing text or searching the library, and buttons must retain focus, labels, tooltips, and announcements.

hardGates.name: Honest Comment capability gating
hardGates.why: The slot must call the registered licensed comment tool when available and remain explicitly disabled—not fake—when it is unavailable.

variants.name: Compose Upstream
variants.thesis: Render the Figma family slots inside tldraw's own DefaultToolbar and route every selection through its stock tool registry; add only the memory, curve, and library gaps.
variants.bestWhen: Reusing the maximum amount of tested tldraw UI and interaction infrastructure is the governing preference.
variants.losesWhen: The toolbar must have zero dependency on DefaultToolbar's extra-chrome DOM/CSS or its responsive overflow behavior.

decisions.label: Mount
decisions.value: Set components.Toolbar to SystemSketchToolbar; that component returns DefaultToolbar with exactly seven custom child slots and minItems/maxItems tuned to the fixed dock.

decisions.label: Stock reuse
decisions.value: Keep DefaultToolbar/OverflowingToolbar, TldrawUiToolbarButton, dropdown/popover/input primitives, useTools, useIsToolSelected, tool analytics/a11y announcements, and the built-in keyboard registry.

decisions.label: Hotkeys
decisions.value: Use TLUiOverrides.tools to wrap rectangle, ellipse, line, and arrow onSelect callbacks. R/O/L remain stock registrations; the overridden A callback recalls or cycles before delegating to the stock arrow action.

decisions.label: Memory
decisions.value: Read current tool and shared styles from the editor. Keep only lastByFamily and straight-vs-curve recall in one namespaced UI preference store shared by both toolbar and overflow render trees.

decisions.label: Curve gap
decisions.value: Register one guarded before-create shape side effect: only when the active tool is Arrow and the UI preset is Curve, change the new stock arrow from bend 0 to the agreed non-zero bend. Elbow uses ArrowShapeKindStyle.

decisions.label: Library
decisions.value: Use tldraw's popover, input, menu lifecycle, and focus behavior; SystemSketch owns the searchable catalog, categories, sidebar-like sizing, and insert commands.

decisions.label: Comment
decisions.value: Call tools.comment when @tldraw/commenting is registered and licensed; otherwise keep the seventh slot present but disabled with explicit entitlement copy.

decisions.label: Main constraint
decisions.value: Scope one CSS rule to hide DefaultToolbar's stock extras/mobile style strip. This is the only deliberate dependency on its current class structure and receives an upgrade smoke test.

keepParts: stock tool callbacks and style state
proof: A focused real-canvas journey presses A, A, R, O, L, switches to Cursor, then presses A and sees the remembered arrow preset in the same family slot.
The same toolbar remains keyboard- and screen-reader-operable when DefaultToolbar moves children into overflow; duplicate render trees share one preference source.
Creating a curve changes only newly created arrows while imported, pasted, duplicated, and programmatically created arrows retain their original bend.
Typing A/R/O/L inside canvas text editing and library search never changes tools.
A tldraw version-bump smoke catches changes to the one scoped extra-chrome selector and seven direct toolbar children.

c1.evidence: Verified public exports cover DefaultToolbar with custom children, OverflowingToolbar, menu/toolbar primitives, useTools, TLUiOverrides, style APIs, and editor side effects.

c2.evidence: The seven family slots and behaviors fit, but hiding DefaultToolbar extras and styling its stock container are constrained adaptations rather than a fully owned pixel shell.

c3.evidence: Behavior uses public APIs; upgrade exposure is limited to one documented stock class/DOM contract for hiding extras and fitting the Figma chrome.

c4.evidence: Tool wrappers and the arrow transition table are pure-testable; the only editor mutation is a type- and preset-guarded before-create handler.

c5.evidence: The first vertical slice composes existing tool callbacks and responsive toolbar behavior instead of building new focus, keyboard, menu, or overflow systems.

g1.evidence: DefaultToolbar accepts seven replacement children; each is a family slot rather than an individual stock-tool row.

g2.evidence: Stock keyboard registrations invoke wrapped R/O/L/A tool items, and the shared preference store owns repeat-A recall.

g3.evidence: The + slot opens a searchable host catalog inside tldraw focus/menu primitives.

g4.evidence: Only component overrides, tool overrides, style APIs, and a side effect are used; preference never enters the board store.

g5.evidence: The built-in tldraw keyboard registry already suppresses shortcuts during editing/open menus and provides toolbar semantics, focus, tooltips, and announcements.

g6.evidence: The slot resolves the real registered comment tool and has a deliberate disabled state when the licensed package is absent.

variants.name: Own the Controller
variants.thesis: Build an exact SystemSketch toolbar shell and explicit command controller from public tldraw primitives, while keeping every canvas action and keyboard registration on the stock editor boundary.
variants.bestWhen: Exact Figma layout, responsive rules, sidebar behavior, and a stable host-owned DOM matter slightly more than maximum DefaultToolbar reuse.
variants.losesWhen: The product is not ready to own toolbar layout, roving focus, overflow decisions, and more browser-level regression coverage.

decisions.label: Mount
decisions.value: Set components.Toolbar to a fully host-owned SystemSketchToolbar built from public TldrawUiToolbar, TldrawUiToolbarButton, dropdown, popover, input, icon, and tooltip primitives.

decisions.label: Controller
decisions.value: Create one createToolbarCommands(editor, preferences) boundary. Both family buttons and TLUiOverrides tool callbacks call these commands, so click and keyboard behavior cannot drift.

decisions.label: Hotkeys
decisions.value: Still retain tldraw's keyboard registry by wrapping the stock tool items; the controller owns repeat-A semantics but does not add a competing document-level keydown listener.

decisions.label: Memory
decisions.value: A pure reducer owns active family, lastByFamily, arrowPreset, and libraryOpen. Editor state remains authoritative for the real active tool; the reducer stores only recall and transient UI state.

decisions.label: Curve gap
decisions.value: Use the same guarded before-create adapter as P1, but drive it from the controller's arrowPreset rather than a thin tool wrapper.

decisions.label: Library
decisions.value: Render a real left aside under the toolbar provider. Own search, categories, focus return, escape/outside dismissal, and insert commands while reusing tldraw button/input/icon primitives.

decisions.label: Responsive
decisions.value: Keep all seven stable slots down to the agreed minimum width, then switch to an explicitly designed compact mode; do not inherit stock overflow or extra controls.

decisions.label: Main constraint
decisions.value: More SystemSketch code becomes responsible for keyboard focus order, collision behavior, coarse-pointer targets, mobile sizing, and visual regressions.

keepParts: one command boundary for click + keyboard
stock tool callbacks and keyboard registry
proof: Golden browser screenshots at wide, compact, and coarse-pointer breakpoints show the exact seven-slot silhouette and no collision with the existing utility strip.
A reducer test covers all transitions, including first A from another tool, repeated A, family recall, and library opening without tool change.
An editor integration journey proves clicks and hotkeys call the same command path and preserve tldraw selection/tool state.
Focus returns to + when the library closes, Escape dismisses it, and search input suppresses canvas shortcuts.
A tldraw upgrade test depends only on public primitive and editor APIs, not DefaultToolbar markup.

c1.evidence: The plan retains tldraw primitives, tools, keyboard registry, styles, editor, and focus helpers, but replaces DefaultToolbar and responsive overflow.

c2.evidence: Owning the DOM, responsive rules, and sidebar removes the extra-chrome and stock-container compromises in P1.

c3.evidence: The integration uses public UI primitives and editor APIs behind one command adapter with no dependency on DefaultToolbar's class structure.

c4.evidence: A pure reducer and single command boundary make tool, recall, and sidebar transitions explicit and independently testable.

c5.evidence: The custom responsive shell, focus behavior, sidebar, and browser coverage must exist before the result is production-complete.

g1.evidence: The host owns the exact seven-slot DOM and responsive design.

g2.evidence: The command reducer defines R/O/L/A and recall as explicit transitions shared by clicks and stock keyboard callbacks.

g3.evidence: The + slot controls a true searchable sidebar with owned focus return.

g4.evidence: The custom layer ends at public editor/tool APIs; toolbar preference remains outside document state.

g5.evidence: The plan includes explicit focus, input suppression, coarse pointer, and accessibility acceptance journeys.

g6.evidence: The real tools.comment entry is used when available, with a labeled disabled state otherwise.

variants.name: Register Preset Tools
variants.thesis: Make Straight Arrow, Curve Arrow, and Elbow Arrow first-class editor tool states, then drive the Figma family slots from a typed tool catalog instead of adapting stock Arrow at creation time.
variants.bestWhen: Arrow presets are the beginning of a larger domain-tool platform whose behaviors must be addressable, scriptable, and testable as first-class tool IDs.
variants.losesWhen: This is only a toolbar interaction and avoiding copied or coupled tool-state logic is more important than a future preset-tool platform.

decisions.label: Mount
decisions.value: Use a catalog-driven host toolbar shell. Every slot resolves a ToolDescriptor with icon, label, shortcut, active predicate, and editor activation command.

decisions.label: Tool layer
decisions.value: Register arrow-straight, arrow-curve, and arrow-elbow StateNode tools plus matching TLUiToolItem entries. Repeated A rotates the registered preset IDs rather than mutating one Arrow preference.

decisions.label: Creation
decisions.value: Each preset tool creates the same stock arrow shape with explicit kind/bend defaults and returns to its own tool ID after an interaction, preserving active feedback without a broad shape side effect.

decisions.label: Memory
decisions.value: The current preset is editor tool state; the catalog stores lastByFamily only for recall after switching families. The board still stores ordinary tldraw arrow shapes, not custom shape types.

decisions.label: Library
decisions.value: Library catalog entries and toolbar entries share the typed descriptor model, allowing future domain objects to expose insert, drag, shortcut, and availability capabilities consistently.

decisions.label: Testing
decisions.value: StateNode tests cover idle → pointing → dragging → complete/cancel/interrupt for every arrow preset, plus binding, snapping, sticky-tool, touch, and selection return behavior.

decisions.label: Main constraint
decisions.value: tldraw's exported ArrowShapeTool is public, but its Pointing flow currently hard-codes onInteractionEnd: arrow. Exact preset identity therefore requires owning or closely mirroring that interaction path.

decisions.label: Use threshold
decisions.value: Do not choose this plan for three arrow icons alone; choose it only if at least two more semantic preset families will need first-class tool states soon.

proof: Each arrow preset remains the active tool across create, complete, cancel, interrupt, sticky-tool, and selection transitions.
Bindings, snapping, arrow labels, touch long-press, precise targeting, undo, and imported stock arrows match the upstream Arrow tool.
R/O/L/A and toolbar clicks resolve through one typed catalog with correct icons and accessibility labels.
The document contains only type: arrow with ordinary kind/bend props, so collaborators without the custom toolbar can still render and edit it.
A pinned tldraw upgrade diff explicitly compares upstream ArrowShapeTool/Pointing behavior before promotion.

c1.evidence: Canvas geometry and shape utilities remain stock, but preset tool states and the catalog duplicate behavior that P1 delegates to the single upstream Arrow tool.

c2.evidence: First-class preset IDs can express exact active state, cycling, recall, and preset creation with no toolbar ambiguity.

c3.evidence: Tool registration is public, but exact interaction parity requires mirroring an upstream Pointing path whose return target is currently hard-coded to arrow.

c4.evidence: Explicit tool IDs and state-node transition tests make every preset behavior observable, although the test matrix is much larger.

c5.evidence: Multiple tool states, a catalog, and parity tests are substantial platform work before the same V1 toolbar journey is complete.

g1.evidence: The catalog renders the same fixed seven family slots.

g2.evidence: R/O/L/A select explicit tool descriptors and Arrow rotation is a first-class tool transition.

g3.evidence: The shared catalog supports a searchable + library and insert commands.

g4.evidence: Tools are registered through public seams and still create ordinary stock arrow shapes; no fork or custom document type is proposed.

g5.evidence: The plan retains tldraw keyboard registration and requires full focus, touch, cancel, and editing-state tests.

g6.evidence: Comment remains a capability-gated descriptor backed by tools.comment.
